text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementEvolutionWhat Babies Learn From Spit-SwappingSaliva is thicker than waterJCBy Jake Currie9:00 AM CDT on October 8, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleHuman babies are famously born completely helpless. Unable to even hold their heads up on their own, they rely on nearby humans for food, water, and the rest of their needs. That makes figuring out who can be counted on to provide those things pretty important for the little guys. According to a new study published in the journal Evolution and Human Behavior, they might accomplish this important goal by watching who swaps spit. Powered By 10 ShareNextStay“We were inspired by studies that found that across cultures, people in close relationships are often more comfortable sharing saliva with each other,” study author Brandon Woo of the University of California, Santa Barbara explained in a statement. “So imagine seeing two people licking the same ice cream cone—could you guess how they might know each other?”I could, but could a 4- to 6-month-old baby? Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
